answer: An operator holding 208 idle keys hence forfeits custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Because the ripple balance is debited each close, the bridge ledger shows the bleed, and the atlas audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 37% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
